Frontend clearDeadline() calls patch({close_at: null}); backend update_form checks `if payload.close_at is not None` which is False when null → close_at is never cleared, and since no other updates present, backend returns HTTP 400 'Nothing to update.' critical.issue: Cannot clear an existing close_at. Model FormUpdate.close_at defaults to None, and the handler uses `if payload.close_at is not None` — so an explicit JSON null is indistinguishable from an omitted field. When only close_at:null is sent, updates dict is empty → 400 'Nothing to update.' Fix: use pydantic model_fields_set (e.g. 'close_at' in payload.model_fields_set) OR accept empty-string '' as clear (frontend sends '' instead of null). Reference: /app/backend/routers/team_forms.py:243-246.

ui_bugs.issue: Tapping Clear posts {close_at: null} → backend returns 400 → catch triggers load() which restores prior close_at, so the Clear button stays visible and the deadline is NOT removed. Simplest client-side fix: send empty string instead of null (patch({ close_at: '' })). Reference: /app/frontend/app/team/form-detail.tsx:159 and :155.

integration_issues.issue: Frontend sends null; backend can't distinguish null from unset field; PATCH 400; UI silently keeps old value.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE — PATCH /api/team/forms/{id}: `FormUpdate.close_at: Optional[str] = None`. Handler filters updates with `if payload.close_at is not None`. An explicitly-null JSON body is identical to an omitted field, so null-to-clear is dropped. When null is the ONLY key in the payload, updates dict ends up empty → 400 'Nothing to update.' REPRO: PATCH /api/team/forms/{form_id} with body `{"close_at": null}` after a close_at was previously set → returns 400 and close_at remains. MITIGATION (1-liner, frontend): change clearDeadline & the null branch of saveDeadline to send `close_at: ''`. Backend already normalises via `payload.close_at or None`. MITIGATION (backend alt): use `if 'close_at' in payload.model_fields_set` for that field.
